summary: Reviewed all six modified node files (developer, qa, reviewer, security_auditor, release_engineer, docs). All acceptance criteria are met: each _build_*_prompt() returns exactly project_path, wp_id, and the verbatim injection-safety warning — nothing more. Code is perfectly uniform across all six files. Ruff passes clean independently verified. Architecture boundary (persona system prompt vs. minimal user-turn context) is correctly implemented. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: All six _build_*_prompt() functions are structurally identical — 8 lines each, same f-string layout, same Unicode escape (\u2014), same !r repr quoting for project_path, same # type: ignore[call-overload] annotation on state.get(). This uniformity is a maintainability asset: any future change to the minimal prompt pattern can be applied mechanically across all six files.

Architecture boundary is correctly enforced: identity declarations and workflow step enumerations live exclusively in persona YAML files loaded by create_stage_node → load_persona(); the user-turn prompt carries only runtime context (project_path, wp_id, injection-safety warning). This matches the intent described in pm.py's module docstring, which explicitly documents this separation.

Module-level docstrings in the six files (especially docs.py which lists a 4-step workflow, and reviewer.py/qa.py which describe pipeline behaviour) accurately describe what the *node* does overall, but do not mention that the user-turn prompt is intentionally minimal. Consider adding a one-liner to each module docstring along the lines of: 'The user-turn prompt provides only runtime context (project path, WP ID, injection-safety warning); all identity and workflow guidance lives in the persona system prompt.' This would help future maintainers understand the design intent at a glance.
